703428.t: From διαβάλλω (diabállō, “to slander”, from δια- (dia-, “through”) + βάλλω (bállō, “to throw”)). For the meaning development, compare Russian кида́ла (kidála), кида́лово (kidálovo) related to кида́ть (kidátʹ).

703417.t: From *δισά (disá), from Proto-Indo-European *dwís (“twice, in two”) (related to δίς (dís, “twice”) and δύο (dúo, “two”)). Cognates include Latin dis- and Gothic 𐌳𐌹𐍃- (dis-).

703478.t: δια- (dĭă-) + Proto-Indo-European *kón-os, from *ken- (“to set oneself in motion”).

703447.t: From διαδέω (diadéō, “to bind round”) + -μα (-ma, result noun suffix).

703411.t: Together with Mycenaean Greek 𐀅𐀗 (da-mo), traceable back to Proto-Hellenic *dā́mos, inherited from Proto-Indo-European *déh₂mos (“part, division”), from *deh₂- (“to share, divide”) + *-mos.

703456.t: From διατίθημι (dĭătĭ́thēmĭ); also analyzable as δια- (dia-) + -θήκη (-thḗkē)

703412.t: From *δημότ-ιος (-ios) with assibilation of *τ > σ, from δημότης (dēmótēs, “one of the people; fellow citizen”) + -ιος (-ios).

703495.t: From δια- (dĭă-) + λέγω (légō, “to say, to speak”).

703460.t: PIE word *dwís Nominal formation from διαιτάω (dĭaitắō, “to treat, handle”).

703410.t: From an earlier unattested *δημιο-ϝεργός (*dēmio-wergós), from a univerbation of δήμια ἔργα (dḗmia érgă).

703481.t: From δια- (dia-, “dia-, through-”) + κόπτω (kóptō, “to strike, cut”).

703401.t: According to Beekes and LIV, from Proto-Indo-European *deyh₂- (“to light up, shine”), and related to δέατο (déato, “seemed”). Compare Sanskrit दीप् (dīp, “to blaze, glow”), and see there for more cognates.

703419.t: From δια- (dĭă-, “in different directions, apart, asunder; dia-”) + βαίνω (baínō, “to walk, step”).

703480.t: From διακόπτω (diakóptō, “to cut in two, cut through”) + -ή (-ḗ). By surface analysis, δια- (dia-, “dia-, through-”) + κοπή (kopḗ, “cutting in pieces”).

703458.t: From διαιρέω (diairéō, “take apart, cleave, divide”) + -σις (-sis), from δια- (dia-, “apart”) + αἱρέω (hairéō, “take, grasp”).

703437.t: From διαγιγνώσκω (dĭăgĭgnṓskō, “distinguish; discern”) + -σις (-sĭs), from δια- (dĭă-) + γιγνώσκω (gĭgnṓskō, “know”).

703461.t: PIE word *dwís Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *dwóh₁ ▲ Proto-Indo-European *trísinflu. Proto-Indo-European *dwísder.

703427.t: From διαβάλλω (diabállō, “to calumniate”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun suffix).

703440.t: From διαγράφω (dĭăgrắphō, “to mark out lines, delineate”) + -ή (-ḗ).

703424.t: From δια- (dia-, “through-, dia-”) + βιβάζω (bibázō, “to cause to mount”).
